text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's keystore rotation + the new L7 firewall rule, eu-west-2 GPU nodes are stalling on node join. Seeing lots of decrypt timeouts in the node bootstrap logs.

dave: saw the same. warm-pool didn't refill. some jobs queued up in the scheduler.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created: region eu-west-2 provisioning failure — node join decrypt errors. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

jing: logs show `aws-kms: decrypt failed: AccessDenied` coming from `node-init` for the ephemeral keystore key ARN. Possibly the rotation created a transient key policy drop.

maria: correct. audit export shows a short window where the new key had a narrower principal list. It lines up with the spike at 02:12 UTC.

ops-lead: what's the impact? Are Dedicated pools affected? Cost hit?

dave: Dedicated reserved pools OK because those nodes use customer-managed keystores. This hit our shared warm pools and on-demand GPU nodes only. Estimated 900 GPU-minutes queued so far (~$150) and several customer requests delayed.

audits: grabbing the KMS key policy diff now. If rotation authored a temporary deny, we need to capture who approved that change in the audit trail.

maria: immediate mitigation idea: revert the key alias to the previous key material or add the node-init role back to the key policy. Which is faster?

jing: revert alias is fastest and safe for a temporary rollback. But we should coordinate with compliance — alias change gets logged but doesn't require rekeying data.

ops-lead: do it. Plan: 1) revert alias to old key 2) restart node-init on the 3 queued warm-pool nodes 3) monitor node join success metric on the infra console (route: /regions/eu-west-2/provisioning). Who runs step 1?

dave: I'll run it. command I'll use: `aws kms update-alias --alias-name alias/ephemeral-keystore --target-key-id <old-key-id>` — will push to runbook and annotate.

maria: also need a firewall check. The new L7 rule we applied yesterday blocks outbound to our keystore proxy on port 8443 from the warm pool subnet under the assumption traffic is internal. That was overly broad.

jing: edge case: SDK falls back to IPv6 resolved endpoint which lives in a different subnet; our L7 rule dropped that. Short fix: add an exception for `keystore-proxy.internal.redwood:8443` in the rule.

dave: alias revert done at 02:40 UTC — aws returned OK. rolling restart of node-init on 3 nodes started.

sre-bot: Probe: node-join-success metric for eu-west-2: 02:45 -> 02:52 shows three successful joins. Warm pool back to target +1.

maria: verified jobs started draining. cost estimate revised to ~$40 incremental for the failed attempts (we preemptively spun up some nodes before rollback).

audits: captured the policy delta and the approving actor: `infra-batch-rotations` job triggered the rotation, PR #8234 merged yesterday by `infra-automation`. We're opening an RCA ticket for change gating.

ops-lead: follow-ups: 1) add gate to rotation job to validate keystore policy includes `role/node-init` (test in staging) 2) tighten L7 rollout: add canary with subset of subnets and keep an allowlist for keystore proxy hostnames 3) add alert on 'node-join-failure' tied to KMS AccessDenied.

jing: I'll make the rotation gate patch and add unit test to simulate policy shrink. PR by EOD.

dave: creating firewall rollback PR to allow keystore-proxy hostnames for warm pools.

sre-bot: Related dashboards: provisioning > node-join-success, warmpool > fill-rate, keystore > decrypt-latency. Saved as watchlist `eu-west-2 keystore regressions`.

maria: thanks team. capturing notes into INC-2026 and assigning RCA to eng-infra/keystore. Please paste any extra logs into the incident thread. :thumbsup:
